newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Top Russian firms say have paid taxes with goods.
newsitem.headline: Top Russian firms say have paid taxes with goods.

text.p: Prominent Russian companies threatened by the government with liquidation said on Thursday that they should not be declared bankrupt because they had already paid their debts -- but not in cash.
Oil firms AO Tatneft and AO Purneftegaz said they had paid off nearly all of their delinquent tax bills with in-kind shipments of refined oil products under a state programme to bring in the harvest.
A representative of car and truckmaker AO Kamaz said it had been freed from tax payments until September 1 by government order and that it would soon close a deal to pay taxes in kind.

"Instead of taxes, we will pay in cars," said spokesman Nail Galiullin by telephone from Kamaz headquarters Naberezhnye Chelny in the southern Volga region. "We have full agreement and practically all of the documents are ready for signing."
The government said on Tuesday that it would take six companies to bankruptcy court within a week if they did not pay outstanding taxes of almost 1.3 trillion roubles ($240 million).
In addition to Tatneft, Purneftegaz and Kamaz, officials cited car maker AO Moskvich, oil refinery AO Krasnodarnefteorgsintez and the Achinsky Glinozyomny Kombinat alumina plant as delinquent payers.
Moscow is trying to get tough on tax collection to bring in cash needed to plug the budget deficit and keep economic reforms on track by non-inflationary means.
Government figures show tax revenues at only 74 percent of targeted levels for the first nine months of this year.
President Boris Yeltsin has created a special tax collection committee to get tough on debtors.
But payment-in-kind is a mechanism international lenders like the World Bank and International Monetary fund do not like.
Many Russian tax-debtors are experiencing a severe cash-flow crisis and complain their tax burden is exorbitantly high, while some senior officials said the planned crackdown was misguided.
"We will not let Rosneft go bankrupt," Fuel and Energy Minister Pyotr Rodionov said on Thursday. State-owned joint stock firm Rosneft owns Purneftegaz and the Krasnodar refinery.
Rosneft spokesman Vladimir Tumarkin said government attempts to force bankruptcy proceedings would sputter out.

A Rosneft statement said Purneftegaz had delivered 285 billion roubles' worth of oil for agricultural uses by September and agreed to deliver another 45 billion of oil products, all against 335 billion roubles in tax arrears.
An official at Tatneft, which said it had supplied 365 billion roubles' of oil towards 407 billion roubles in taxes, said the finance ministry would straighten out the problem.
"We expect to receive tax credits and confirmation that we paid our debts with payments in goods," the official said.
Jim Nail, head of research at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell's Moscow office, said Russia was unlikely to succeed in getting companies or anyone else in Russia to cough up tax arrears.
"The liquidity squeeze is one of the key problems facing the whole country -- and the government and the banks," he said.
Since the government and companies faced the same problems, they would have to look at common solutions.
"The government is going to have to go to outside sources for capital, and the companies are going to have to go to outside funds for capital as far as they can."
-- Moscow Newsroom, +7095 941 8520 ($1 = 5,434 roubles)
